2019_130_022619regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of February 26, 2019 at the Services Building. It sets the district's enrollment posture for 2019-2020 — closing Barnard, Bemis, Schroeder, Boulan Park and both high schools to open enrollment except for up to 25 incoming ninth graders transferring to Athens, while opening a limited Schools of Choice program for 50 kindergarten, one first grade and 20 middle school seats — and awards the two largest remaining pieces of the new preschool: $702,576.00 of playground construction to Rolar, Inc. and $482,495.76 of furnishings. It also carries the December 2018 Treasurer's Report with total disbursements in period of $8,420,287.20.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting, February 26, 2019, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois.

**Recognition**
Three items: the Fall 2018 All-State Athletes; a Mission Moment on elementary student artwork created for the new TSD Preschool; and Principal Appreciation Month.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the January 8 workshop and the January 15 organizational and regular meeting, the December 2018 Treasurer's Report, and second reading and adoption of new and revised board policies reviewed by the Board Policy Committee for compliance with the Revised School Code.

**Treasurer's Report — December 2018**
General Fund check disbursements total $4,103,654.39 and total disbursements in period are $8,420,287.20. At December 31, 2018 the General Fund balance stands at $18,641,192, consolidated Debt Service at $8,096,255 and consolidated Special Revenue at $2,454,680.

**Curriculum — who may enroll in 2019-2020**
Dr. Machesky presents enrollment projections for 2019-2020 and beyond, built on an analysis of the district's enrollment history prepared by Dr. Fred Ignatovich of Stanfred Consultants.

On the strength of those projections, administration recommends closing several buildings to open enrollment. Barnard, Bemis, Schroeder and Boulan Park are closed on total enrollment and physical space constraints. Athens and Troy High have been closed for several years as the district works to maximize each building's enrollment, and both are closed again — with one exception: **not more than 25 incoming ninth grade students who live in the Troy High attendance area but wish to attend Athens**, with applications accepted during a two-week window at the beginning of March. Students with siblings already at Athens or Troy High in grades 9 through 11 may open enroll to remain for the year.

Separately, and in the opposite direction, the Board adopts the annual Schools of Choice resolution required by state law. Under Section 105 and 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, the district will accept applications for a limited program for 2019-2020 covering **50 kindergarten, 1 first grade and 20 total 6th-8th grade nonresident students** at Baker, Larson and Smith middle schools, open to students from districts within or outside Oakland County where that intermediate school district is contiguous with Oakland ISD boundaries.

**Business — finishing the preschool**
RFP 9873, Bid Pack 5 of the Early Childcare Center project, sought competitive bids for playground area construction — site construction, playground equipment and site amenities for the new building. Five bidders responded, and Rob Carson and Barton Malow recommend Rolar, Inc. on low bid for its category, including four alternates, at $702,576.00 from the Early Childcare Center Fund.

Furnishings for the preschool were sourced and priced through cooperative bid contracts and reviewed by Rob Carson, Kris Griffor, Erin Keyser and TMP Architecture, awarded at $482,495.76 from the Early Childhood Center Fund with the resolution made part of the official minutes.

**Other**
The Board casts its ballot in the 2019 MASB Board of Directors' election for Region 8, a three-year term with one seat. The candidates are Joshua Denzler (Lake Shore Public Schools, Macomb County), **Steve Gottlieb (Troy School District, Oakland County)**, Birgit McQuiston (Lake Orion Community Schools), Darlene Pomponio, Ph.D. (Southgate Community Schools, Wayne County), Angie Smith (Farmington Public Schools), Michael Swiecki (Wyandotte Public Schools, Wayne County) and Regina Williams (Harper Woods School District, Wayne County).

Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, February 26, 2019, 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The agenda is: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Recognition — A. All-State Athletes Fall 2018, B. Mission Moment: Elementary Student Artwork for TSD Preschool, C. Principal Appreciation Month; 3. Additions & Deletions; 4. Public Communication (agenda items); 5. General – Consent Agenda — A. Minutes of the January 8, 2019 workshop, B. Minutes of the January 15, 2019 organizational and regular meeting, C. Treasurer's Report – December 2018, D. Second Reading and Adoption of New/Revised Board Policies; 6. Personnel; 7. Curriculum — A. Report: Enrollment Projections, B. Consideration: Schools Closed to Open Enrollment, C. Report: Schools of Choice 105 & 105C, D. Consideration: Schools of Choice 105 & 105C; 8. Business — A. TSD Preschool Playground, B. TSD Preschool Furniture; 9. Public Communication (non-agenda items); 10. Other — A. 2019 MASB Board of Directors' Election; 11. Adjournment. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition.** The evening opens with recognition of the All-State Athletes for Fall 2018, a Mission Moment featuring elementary student artwork created for the new Troy School District Preschool, and Principal Appreciation Month.

**Consent agenda.** Minutes of the January 8, 2019 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the January 15, 2019 Board of Education Organizational and Regular Meeting; the Treasurer's Report for December 2018; and second reading and adoption of new and revised board policies. The policy item records that members of the Board Policy Committee reviewed the listed policies against the Revised School Code and that the first reading of the revised and additional policies was conducted at the prior meeting.

**Treasurer's Report, December 2018.** General Fund check disbursements total $4,103,654.39, and total disbursements in period — check disbursements together with ACH debits, outgoing wire transfers, P-Card purchases and prior period void disbursements — come to $8,420,287.20. The summary revenue and expense budget reports for the period ending December 31, 2018 give a General Fund balance of $18,641,192, a consolidated Debt Service Funds balance of $8,096,255 and a consolidated Special Revenue Funds balance of $2,454,680. The middle sections of the packet carry the December check register run by fund.

**Curriculum 7.A: enrollment projections.** Dr. Machesky presents to the Board on enrollment projections for the 2019-2020 school year and beyond. The analysis of the district's enrollment history and projections was provided by Dr. Fred Ignatovich of Stanfred Consultants.

**Curriculum 7.B: schools closed to open enrollment for 2019-2020.** Administration reports having reviewed enrollment for the elementary, middle and high school attendance areas. Because of the elementary and middle school buildings' total student enrollment and physical space constraints, it recommends that Barnard, Bemis, Schroeder and Boulan Park schools be closed to open enrollment. It notes that the district's goal for Athens and Troy High has been to maximize each building's enrollment, which has resulted in both being closed to open enrollment for the past several years, and that based on current projections for 2019-2020 both should be closed again — with the exception of not more than twenty-five incoming ninth grade students who reside in the Troy High School attendance area but wish to attend Athens High School. Applications for those twenty-five spots at Athens will be accepted during a two-week window at the beginning of March.

The resolution closes Barnard, Bemis, Schroeder and Boulan Park schools as well as Athens and Troy High Schools to open enrollment for the 2019-2020 school year, with that twenty-five-student exception, and provides that students with siblings attending Athens and Troy High who are currently enrolled in grades 9 through 11 will be allowed to open enroll to remain for the 2019-2020 school year.

**Curriculum 7.C and 7.D: Schools of Choice under Sections 105 and 105c.** A report precedes the resolution. In accordance with Michigan state law, school districts must pass a resolution each school year if they intend to participate in a Schools of Choice program. The item anticipates that a limited number of seats will be available for 2019-2020 for kindergarten, first grade, and grades six through eight at Baker, Larson and Smith Middle Schools, and proposes a resolution for fifty kindergarten, one first grade, and twenty total sixth through eighth grade nonresident students who attend a school district within or outside of Oakland County, provided that intermediate school district is contiguous with the Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries.

The resolution accordingly provides that the Board of Education, exercising the option permitted by Section 105 and 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, will accept applications for a Limited Schools of Choice program for the 2019-2020 school year for fifty kindergarten, one first grade and twenty total sixth through eighth grade nonresident students on those terms. Read alongside item 7.B, the two resolutions set the district's enrollment posture from both directions in a single meeting: closing the buildings under space pressure while opening a bounded number of seats where capacity exists.

**Business 8.A: preschool playground.** An RFP was issued for competitive bids on playground area construction as part of the Troy School District Preschool project, with responses reviewed by Rob Carson, Director of Operations, and Barton Malow Company. Rob Carson's February 21, 2019 memorandum to Rick West, covering RFP 9873, Bid Pack 5 of the ECC Building Project, records that the RFP produced five bidders and that the scope of work is site construction, playground equipment and site amenities for the new Early Childcare Center building, with an attached bid summary detailing four alternates he recommends as part of the RFP. He recommends, on low bid for the category, category 116000 Playground Equipment to Rolar, Inc. including alternates A1, A2, A3 and A4 at $702,576.00. The resolution awards the playground area construction to Rolar, Inc. in the amount of $702,576.00 as an expenditure of the Early Childcare Center Fund.

**Business 8.B: preschool furnishings.** Quotations were received for competitive pricing on furnishings for the Troy School District Preschool. The recommended items were sourced and priced through cooperative bid contracts and reviewed by Rob Carson, Director of Operations; Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent for Elementary Instruction; Erin Keyser, Director of Early Childhood Programs; and TMP Architecture. The resolution awards the furnishings as attached in the amount of $482,495.76 as an expenditure of the Early Childhood Center Fund, with the resolution made a part of the official minutes of the February 26, 2019 regular meeting; the attached award schedule assigns vendors by category on low bid.

**Other 10.A: 2019 MASB Board of Directors' election.** Biographical data for the candidates is attached for the Board's review. The Region 8 seat is a three-year term with one seat, and the candidates are Joshua Denzler of Lake Shore Public Schools in Macomb County; Steve Gottlieb of the Troy School District, Oakland County; Birgit McQuiston of Lake Orion Community Schools, Oakland County; Darlene Pomponio, Ph.D. of Southgate Community Schools, Wayne County; Angie Smith of Farmington Public Schools, Oakland County; Michael Swiecki of Wyandotte Public Schools, Wayne County; and Regina Williams of Harper Woods School District, Wayne County. The resolution casts the Troy Board of Education's ballot for one candidate to serve on the 2019 Michigan Association of School Boards' Board of Directors for the Region 8 three-year term — an election in which one of the district's own trustees, Steve Gottlieb, is a candidate.
